text:
laura_infra: Heads-up — after last night's BIOS+FW batch in ap-south1 a subset of racks (~20) are hitting TPM lockdowns during POST. Nodes go into maintenance and GPUs leave the k8s pools. Not a secureboot toggle, looks like TPM attestation failure from the new firmware.

sam_oncall: which racks? are GPU jobs failing immediately or hitting delete/evict? any customer-facing alerts?

laura_infra: racks: ap-s1-rack-12/*, -13/*, -14/* mostly in cluster-gpu-ap-s1. Jobs are failing to schedule because nodes are NotReady or cordoned by node-problem-detector. No external customer alert yet but internal capacity for Dedicated customers degraded ~18%.

ops_robot: [ALERT] nodepool cluster-gpu-ap-s1 reduced healthy nodes from 420 -> 402 (18 nodes removed) — 2026-03-21T02:10Z

mina_fw: I rolled out TPM firmware v1.2.3->1.3.0 last night with the lockdown flag enabled by default on certain OEM SKUs (we thought it would be safe). There's one change in the attestation handshake that could reject older BIOS microcode.

nate_sre: can someone run a quick check on a dead node? ssh jump into ap-s1-admin and paste:

```
ssh ap-s1-admin
for n in ap-s1-rack-12-node{01..05}; do ssh $n "dmesg | grep -i tpm || echo no-tpm-log"; done
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide | grep NotReady
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P '***' mc info
```

laura_infra: ran it on 12-01. dmesg shows: "tpm: TPM 2.0 event log: malformed attestation". ipmitool returns TPM device present but attestation status FAILED.

mina_fw: That matches the handshake mismatch. We introduced a stricter PCR policy in 1.3.0 to mitigate a vuln; apparently some boards have older PCR masks.

sam_oncall: propose immediate steps: 1) pause firmware rollout globally, 2) canary rollback firmware to 1.2.3 on 4 racks, 3) unschedule non-critical jobs and shift Dedicated workloads to eu-west temporary pools. Thoughts?

jess_prod: if we shift to eu-west, customers on Dedicated capacity in AP-S will see latency changes — need to flag impacted customers. Also cost: cross-region repinning and reserved capacity will eat margin.

nate_sre: can we avoid cross-region by draining affected racks and rebalancing within ap-south1? current spare capacity is low. Draining will take down long-running jobs. If we spin new instances in eu-west, estimate +25% per-token cost for inference due to egress and preemption risk.

laura_infra: actioning pause on rollout now. Mina, can you prepare a rollback image for 1.2.3 that we can push via OOB to the 4 canary racks? Runbook snippet:

```
# rollback via jump host
oobctl --rack ap-s1-rack-13 --action flash --image firmware-bmc-1.2.3.bin --reboot
wait_for_nodes ap-s1-rack-13 30m
```

mina_fw: will build and sign rollback image. ETA 20m. note: we need HSM key approval for signed image due to new sig policy. I'm opening a hot ticket with security for expedited sign-off.

ops_robot: [INFO] firmware-rollout: paused by laura_infra (runbook step 1) — 2026-03-21T02:14Z

sam_oncall: Nate/Laura — if rollback doesn't restore attestation, fallback plan is to set BIOS TPM lockdown override (temporarily clear lockdown flag) via ipmi script. That is invasive and needs restart of VM workloads. We should avoid if rollback works.

nate_sre: noted. I'll prepare cordon/drain playbooks and a quick capacity projection. If we move 18 nodes' worth of GPUs to eu-west, scheduler will preempt spot instances elsewhere; expect 12-18h to stabilize.

laura_infra: customers affected: internal list shows 3 Dedicated teams currently >75% load on ap-s1 cluster. Jess, please draft message to those teams explaining temporary capacity hit and we may reroute to eu-west.

jess_prod: on it. also prepare a short FAQ: what this means for SLAs and cost.

mina_fw: rollback image ready and signed. starting canary flash on ap-s1-rack-13 now. will post logs here.

laura_infra: canary started. ops: will watch node rejoin, run kubelet health checks and node-level e2e quick test.

ops_robot: [INFO] ap-s1-rack-13 flash started 2026-03-21T02:28Z

laura_infra: if canary passes we roll back the rest of the rolled-out racks in waves of 4 with 10m gap. If canary fails, we will enable the BIOS override and begin a controlled reboot window with customer notifications.

sam_oncall: capturing this as an incident. I'll create a postmortem template and assign owners: firmware=mina_fw, infra=laura_infra, sres=nate_sre, comms=jess_prod.

laura_infra: thanks — keeping thread updates here. :thumbsup:
